newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Chemical companies worth 450 mln punts to Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Chemical companies worth 450 mln punts to Ireland.

text.p: Irish-based pharmaceutical and chemical manufacturing companies are worth over 450 million punts to Ireland's economy, a study released on Wednesday said.

The first linkage study of the industry said members of the Irish Pharmaceutical and Chemical Manufacturers Federation (IPCMF) had spent a total of 1.04 billion punts on supplies and services in 1995.
Of this total, 457 million Irish pounds was spent in Ireland, 366 million Irish pounds in the rest of the European Union and 217 million Irish pounds in the rest of the world, the study said.
"This puts the amount of business placed with local suppliers as 44 percent of total, which is a significant amount," the study said.
Imports totalled 509 million Irish pounds and the study found that the main reason for sourcing overseas was a lack of availability.

"Now that this important survey has identified potential gaps in the market for Irish suppliers we intend to work closely with Forbairt (Ireland's industrial development agency) to establish if there is a real market in the gap for Irish companies," Matt Moran, IPCMF Director, said.

"To help achieve this we have established a linkage steering group which will work closely with Forbairt personnel. The first area we will be studying is that of packaging where currently over 23 million Irish pounds worth of materials are imported into the country," he added.
